title: SAP weighing at least 10,000 job cuts as it refocuses on AI
dek: Bloomberg reports SAP is planning large workforce reductions as it reshapes its software business around artificial intelligence.
body:
SAP is reportedly planning to cut at least 10,000 jobs as the company reshapes its software business around artificial intelligence, Bloomberg reported and CNBC relayed. The story is unfolding through reporting rather than an official company announcement.

## Why it matters

A reduction of this scale would be one of the largest workforce moves tied explicitly to an AI strategy at a major enterprise software vendor. The report frames the cuts as part of a companywide shift to structure SAP’s products and operations around AI, which could affect product roadmaps, engineering teams and customer-facing roles.

Details about the financial scale, timelines, affected regions, or which product teams would be targeted are not included in the reporting. There is no public SAP statement attached to the report in the material provided here.

## The details

- Bloomberg reported SAP is weighing cuts of at least 10,000 jobs. CNBC published the report.
- The job reductions are described as part of a reshaping of SAP’s software business around AI. 
- The information is based on reporting; no company confirmation is included in the provided material.
- The reporting does not specify which countries, business units, or employee levels would be affected.
- The reporting does not disclose timing, cost savings targets, or expected impact on customers.

## What to watch

Watch for an official statement from SAP confirming the plan and providing specifics on numbers, timing and which teams are affected. Monitor follow-up reporting from Bloomberg and CNBC for additional sourcing, and look for any regulatory filings or filings in jurisdictions where SAP operates that would reflect workforce reductions.

Source: reporting by CNBC.
author: Kelvane Club Desk
